questions.text: What did Professor Aidarov ask students to write about?
opts: Things they have and haven't done
questions.correct: Things they have and haven't done
questions.hint: "Write a personal reflection on their life experiences — the things they have done and haven't done yet."

questions.text: Amir has finished the Aitmatov novel.
questions.hint: "I've started and abandoned the same Aitmatov novel three times." — he hasn't finished it yet.

questions.text: How many mountains has Rustam climbed?
questions.hint: "He has climbed three different mountains in Kazakhstan."

questions.text: Zhibek has trained more than ___ hours for volleyball.
questions.hint: "I've trained more than five thousand hours to become a volleyball player."

questions.text: What final task did Professor Aidarov give the class?
questions.hint: "He then asked the class to write one more sentence — about what they are going to do next."

questions.text: Rustam has flown on aeroplanes many times.
questions.hint: "I've never been on an aeroplane."

questions.text: How many times has Kamila been to Almaty?
questions.hint: "Yes — I've been there three times."

questions.text: How long has Zhibek been playing volleyball?
questions.hint: "I've been playing since I was nine years old. So — almost fifteen years."

questions.text: In the radio interview, one of Zhibek's research papers has been accepted for ___.
questions.hint: "one of them has been accepted for publication."

questions.text: Rustam has been to Almaty before.
questions.hint: "I've never been there. I've always wanted to go but never had the chance."

questions.text: In the interview, what has Zhibek discovered about herself?
opts: She loves sports science and research
questions.correct: She loves sports science and research
questions.hint: "I've started reading research papers on training methodology. I've realised that what I want isn't just to play."

questions.text: How long has Rustam known Zhibek?
questions.hint: "I've known her since secondary school."

questions.text: "She ___ two championships." (no specific time)
questions.hint: No specific time → Present Perfect. "She has won two championships." ✅

questions.text: "He ___ the competition last year." (specific time)
questions.hint: "last year" = specific past time → Past Simple. "He won last year." ✅

questions.text: "write → wrote → ___" (past participle)
questions.hint: "write → wrote → written" (irregular). "She has WRITTEN two papers." ✅

questions.text: "She's ___ to Almaty." (she went and came back — NOT still there)
questions.hint: "have BEEN to" = visited and returned. "She's been to Almaty." ✅

questions.text: "___ you ever ___ (be) abroad?" (general experience)
questions.hint: "ever" → PP. "Have you ever been abroad?" ✅

questions.text: "I have seen him yesterday" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "I saw him yesterday." — "yesterday" = specific past time → ALWAYS Past Simple!

questions.text: "She ___ (already / apply) for the master's." (PP + already)
questions.hint: "already" + PP: "She's already applied." ✅ (position: before the past participle)

questions.text: "give → gave → ___" (past participle)
questions.hint: "give → gave → given" (irregular). "She has GIVEN a speech." ✅

questions.text: "He has contributed to an open-source project." "Contribute" means:
opts: give something to help achieve a result
questions.correct: give something to help achieve a result
questions.hint: "contribute" = to give time, effort, or input to something. "contributed to" = helped with.

questions.text: He has started and ___ the same novel three times.
questions.hint: "abandon" = to stop doing something without finishing it.

questions.text: "That was a remarkable achievement." "Remarkable" means:
questions.hint: "remarkable" = unusual or surprising in a way that causes admiration. Notable.

questions.text: "He accidentally attended the wedding." "Accidentally" means:
questions.hint: "accidentally" = by chance, without planning or intending to.

questions.text: "She's maintained a GPA above 3.8." "Maintain" means:
opts: keep at the same level consistently
questions.correct: keep at the same level consistently
questions.hint: "maintain" = to keep something at the same standard over time, consistently.
